predictions.selection_reason: user-controlled path input -> traverses object hierarchy -> deletes arbitrary property
predictions.source_summary: The `path` parameter is user-controlled input that specifies which property to delete. The path is split by dots to traverse nested object properties.
predictions.sink_summary: The `delete obj[attr]` operation removes a property from an object at the specified path location in the object hierarchy.
predictions.guard_summary: No validation or sanitization of the path input. The function only checks if intermediate properties exist (`if (!obj[seg]) return;`) but doesn't validate path segments for security-sensitive patterns like `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`.
predictions.risk_pattern: User-controlled path input traverses object hierarchy to delete arbitrary properties without validation, potentially allowing deletion of security-critical properties or prototype pollution.
predictions.context_summary: Utility module providing set, get, and delete operations for nested object properties using dot notation paths. The delete function allows removing properties at arbitrary depths.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
top_sast_rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-1321 prototype-pollution __proto__ constructor prototype object-key property-key merge assign recursive-merge
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject prototype keys and use schema-constrained object updates.

top_sast_rules.description: If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Remove unused variables that may contain sensitive data. Use static analysis tools to identify unused code. Review code for potential logic errors.

top_sast_rules.description: Sensitive cookies set by a server can be read by the client if the `httpOnly` flag is not set.
